prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1203; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from insured. Low-speed head-on collision reported at intersection, both vehicles drivable. Insured reports neck pain and stiffness. Vehicle for other party is being towed. Opened bodily injury and property damage features. Assigned to field adjuster for vehicle inspection.

Entry 2: Field inspection completed on insured vehicle. Front bumper cover cracked, hood latch misaligned, minor radiator support damage. Photos uploaded to file. Estimate requested from body shop. Other driver's vehicle has rear-end crush consistent with a low-speed impact on the front. Police report obtained and reviewed; no citations issued.

Entry 3: Notice of representation received. Claimant is represented by counsel, who has requested that all future contact go through their office. Diary set to confirm the claimant's medical providers and treatment dates. Letter of representation filed with the claim. Phone contact with claimant discontinued per attorney request.

Entry 4: Records requested from claimant's primary care office and urgent care facility for treatment following the collision. Diagnosis on initial visit noted as cervical strain. Treatment includes physical therapy referral and prescribed muscle relaxants. Reviewed photos and repair estimate; liability appears probable for the at-fault driver based on the statement and damage pattern. Supervisor notified of representation and open injury reserve.

Entry 5: Received physical therapy progress notes from counsel's office. Patient reports improving range of motion and decreasing pain. Injury file updated with medical summary. Reserve reviewed and adjusted per current treatment plan. Next step is to wait for final treatment report and itemized bills before evaluating settlement posture. File remains open and diaried for follow-up in thirty days.
